data.name: Geneforge 1
data.detailed_description:
Geneforge é um jogo do tipo Indie fantasy role-playing, o primeiro jogo na pentalogia Geneforge Saga. Apresenta um mundo enorme, a possibilidade de criar o teu próprio exército de criaturas letais e totalmente obedientes, e adversários astutos controlados pelo computador que conseguem ir em patrulhas, perseguir-te e chamar por ajuda.

Geneforge possui um enredo enorme e aberto. Tu tens a liberdade para escolher o teu próprio caminho e decidir como é que a história se desenrolará. Tu podes lutar contra o senhor do mal ou juntar-te a ele. Tu podes ajudar os camponeses ou atormentá-los. Tu podes ser o herói corajoso ou podes só tentar fugir. Não importa o que escolheres, Geneforge oferece uma aventura enorme com bastante valor de repetição.

reviews.review:
Geneforge is a classic computer role-playing game developed and published by Spiderweb Software that continues to stand out thanks to its imaginative setting and emphasis on player freedom. Rather than placing players in the role of a traditional fantasy warrior, the game casts them as a Shaper, a member of a powerful order capable of creating living beings through magical science. This unique premise immediately separates the game from more conventional RPGs, introducing a world where knowledge, experimentation, and authority are just as important as swords and spells. Despite its age, the game's original ideas remain compelling, delivering an adventure built around choice, consequence, and discovery instead of flashy presentation.

The story begins when the protagonist becomes stranded on an isolated island once reserved for the Shapers' secret experiments. What initially appears to be an abandoned land gradually reveals itself as a place filled with dangerous creations, political conflict, forgotten laboratories, and hidden truths. As players uncover the island's history, they encounter numerous factions with opposing beliefs about power and freedom. The narrative refuses to divide characters into simple heroes and villains, instead presenting morally complex situations where every alliance and decision can significantly alter the course of the adventure. Multiple endings and branching questlines encourage thoughtful decision-making, making every major choice feel meaningful rather than cosmetic.

Combat unfolds through a tactical turn-based system that rewards careful planning over quick reflexes. The defining gameplay mechanic revolves around the ability to create and command living creatures that fight alongside the player. These summoned allies come in different forms, each offering unique strengths that can complement various playstyles. Some players may build an overwhelming army of creations to dominate battles, while others may focus on mastering magic, diplomacy, stealth, or personal combat abilities. Character progression offers considerable flexibility through a wide range of skills and specializations, allowing players to shape their own approach to exploration and conflict. This level of customization ensures that each playthrough can feel noticeably different from the last.

Exploration is another major highlight, with the game featuring a large world composed of dozens of interconnected locations filled with hidden treasures, optional quests, puzzles, and valuable lore. Every region contributes to the larger narrative, revealing new details about the island's past while presenting opportunities to strengthen the player's character and influence the surrounding world. Curiosity is consistently rewarded, whether through powerful equipment, additional story content, or encounters that reshape relationships with the game's various factions. The campaign offers dozens of hours of gameplay, and its branching structure provides strong replay value for those interested in pursuing different choices and uncovering alternate outcomes.

From a technical standpoint, Geneforge clearly reflects the era in which it was created. Its visuals are simple, animations are modest, and environmental detail is limited compared to modern role-playing games. However, these shortcomings are offset by excellent world-building, thoughtful writing, and gameplay systems that remain surprisingly deep. The interface is practical and easy to understand, allowing players to focus on exploration, tactical encounters, and character development without unnecessary complexity. The atmosphere is further supported by subtle audio design that reinforces the mysterious and often unsettling nature of the island without distracting from the gameplay itself.

Geneforge succeeds because it places player agency at the center of the experience. Rather than leading players down a fixed path, it encourages experimentation, independent thinking, and difficult moral decisions that genuinely influence both the narrative and the world around them. Its innovative creature creation mechanics, extensive customization, and richly branching storyline continue to make it one of the more distinctive classic RPGs available. While newcomers may need time to adjust to its dated presentation, those who value meaningful choices, strategic gameplay, and deep storytelling will discover a rewarding adventure that has aged far better than its visuals might suggest.

Rating: 8/10
